stories.headline: Putin seeks new tax revenue to fund Russia's war as budget deficit swells
stories.title: Putin seeks new tax revenue to fund Russia's war as budget deficit swells
stories.summary: With Russia's invasion of Ukraine intensifying the strain on state finances, President Vladimir Putin is reaching for cash to fund his government and the war, squeezing tax revenue from an economy that's increasingly skewed toward the military - while civilian needs take a back seat. The country's 2027-2029 state budget, which will be taken up Thursday in the rubber-stamp parliament, is accompanied by a string of tax hikes announced after the September parliamentary elections. While last year the Kremlin went for a broad tax increase, raising value-added taxes at the cash register and making more small businesses pay VAT, this cash grab hits a narrower segment: mining companies and better-off citizens with investment income, property sales and bank accounts. The budget deficit this year has swelled beyond forecasts due to lavish military spending and tepid economic growth amid sanctions, high interest rates for non-military companies, labour shortages and Ukrainian strikes on oil ..

stories.headline: HM Shah speaks to Odisha CM, assures comprehensive assistance for cyclone relief
stories.title: HM Shah speaks to Odisha CM, assures comprehensive assistance for cyclone relief
stories.summary: CM Majhi also apprised the Union Home Minister of the extensive impact of cyclone Arnab on Odisha, particularly the southern parts of the state, during their telephonic conversation.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: CM Majhi also apprised the Union Home Minister of the extensive impact of cyclone Arnab on Odisha, particularly the southern parts of the state, during their telephonic conversation.

Bhubaneswar: Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke to Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and assured all possible assistance to the state in dealing with the devastating impact of severe cyclonic storm 'Arnab', which hit the neighbouring Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28.

Referring to the conversation over the phone with HM Shah, CM Majhi wrote on his X handle on Thursday, “Spoke with Hon’ble Union Home Minister Shri@AmitShah Ji and briefed him on the impact of #CycloneArnab across Odisha, the prevailing situation in affected districts, and the relief and restoration measures being undertaken by the State Government.”
Notably, cyclone-induced incessant rainfall triggered severe flooding and massive landslides across parts of South Odisha, affecting thousands and damaging houses, roads and vast paddy fields.
Several areas were cut off after roads and bridges were washed away, while people were stranded in southern districts, particularly Ganjam and Gajapati.
Several teams of Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF), Odisha Fire Services personnel and the National Disaster Response Force are engaged in rescue and relief operations in the affected areas.
“He (Shah) assured all possible assistance to Odisha in the wake of the cyclone.

The support and cooperation of the Government of India will further strengthen our efforts to protect lives, support affected families and expedite relief, rehabilitation and restoration across the State,” CM Majhi added.
The Chief Minister thanked the Union Home Minister for the Central government’s support and cooperation for the state during the emergency situation.
“Grateful to Hon’ble Union Home Minister Shri@AmitShahJi for assuring all possible assistance to Odisha in the wake of Cyclone Arnab.
The support and cooperation of the Government of India will strengthen our efforts to ensure the safety and well-being of every Odia,” CM Majhi noted.

stories.headline: Cyclone ‘Arnab’: 64 train services cancelled on October 27 and 28
stories.title: Cyclone ‘Arnab’: 64 train services cancelled on October 27 and 28
stories.summary: Long-distance express trains connecting Telangana with coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha among those affected; passengers advised to check status before travel
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Railway authorities have cancelled 64 train services scheduled to operate on October 27 and 28 as a precautionary measure in view of the anticipated impact of Cyclone Arnab, prioritising passenger safety amid forecasts of heavy rainfall and strong winds along the Andhra Pradesh coast.

The cancellations include 53 passenger and other services operating across the coastal Andhra Pradesh network and 11 express and special train services connecting Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

The affected routes include Vijayawada–Rajahmundry, Vijayawada–Narasapur, Vijayawada–Machilipatnam, Machilipatnam–Gudivada, Kakinada Port–Visakhapatnam, Bhimavaram–Nidadavolu, Guntur–Repalle and Visakhapatnam–Parvatipuram.

Among the major express trains cancelled on October 27 are the Falaknuma Superfast Express (12704) from Secunderabad to Howrah, New Visakha Express (17016) from Secunderabad to Bhubaneswar, Godavari Superfast Express (12728) from Hyderabad to Visakhapatnam, Visakhapatnam Superfast Express (12862) from Mahabubnagar to Visakhapatnam and Garib Rath Superfast Express (12740) from Secunderabad to Visakhapatnam.

Other affected services include the Cocanada Superfast Express (12776) from Lingampalli to Kakinada Town, Gowthami Superfast Express (12738) from Lingampalli to Kakinada Port, Lingampalli–Narasapur Express (17256) and Nagavalli Superfast Express (20810) from Hazur Sahib Nanded to Sambalpur.
The Charlapalli–Srikakulam Road Special (07037), scheduled to leave on October 27, has also been cancelled.
Its return service, the Srikakulam Road–Charlapalli Special (07038), scheduled to leave on October 28, has been withdrawn as well.
Several passenger services connecting Vijayawada, Rajahmundry, Narsapur, Machilipatnam, Gudivada, Bhimavaram, Kakinada Port, Guntur, Repalle and Tenali have been cancelled on one or both days.
Services between Visakhapatnam and Kakinada Port and between Parvatipuram and Visakhapatnam have also been affected.
The cancellations are part of precautionary measures taken ahead of the expected adverse weather conditions.
Passengers have been advised to check the latest train-running information through official railway enquiry channels before leaving for their stations.

Railway authorities have urged passengers to verify the cancellation status of their specific trains before commencing their journeys, as further changes may be announced depending on weather conditions.

stories.title: Cyclone Arnab effect: Rain intensifies in parts of Jharkhand, to continue till October 30
stories.summary: An ‘Orange’ alert of heavy rainfall has been issued for Garhwa, Palamu, Latehar, Lohardaga, Gumla and Simdega till 8.30 a.m. on October 30
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Rain intensified in parts of Jharkhand on Thursday (October 29, 2026), and the weather department has issued an alert for a downpour till next morning under the influence of "very severe" cyclonic storm Arnab that made landfall along the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday (October 28, 2026).

Gudabanda in East Singhbhum district recorded the highest 71.4 mm rainfall since Wednesday (October 28, 2026) evening, followed by Manjhari in West Singhbhum district at 64 mm, the weather department in Ranchi said.
Ranchi registered 26.2 mm of rainfall, while Chaibasa recorded 60 mm of rain during the period.
"Rain will continue on Thursday [October 29, 2026] with some districts experiencing heavy to very heavy rainfall.
However, the impact will vary by region.
For instance, the effect will be less pronounced in the Santhal region, where there is no alert for heavy rainfall," said Abhishek Anand, the Deputy Director at the Ranchi Meteorological Centre.
An 'Orange' alert of heavy rainfall has been issued for Garhwa, Palamu, Latehar, Lohardaga, Gumla and Simdega till 8.30 a.m. on Friday (October 30, 2026).

A 'yellow' alert, advising people to stay updated about the weather, has been issued for Chatra, Koderma, Hazaribag, Ramgarh, Ranchi, Khunti, Saraikela-Kharsawan, and East and West Singhbhum districts.
"The cyclonic weather system will weaken by October 30 and move a bit away from Jharkhand.
There is no warning for Friday [October 30, 2026].
Light to moderate rainfall is expected during the first half of Friday [October 30, 2026] in the districts of the northwest and those adjacent to the north," Mr. Anand said.
Several districts, including Ranchi, West Singhbhum, East Singhbhum and Simdega, ordered school closure on October 28 and 29 in view of the cyclone.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab claims five lives in Andhra Pradesh; Naidu announces relief package
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab claims five lives in Andhra Pradesh; Naidu announces relief package
stories.summary: ₹5 lakh ex gratia for each victim; aid announced for farmers, fishermen, households and businesses
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Arnab claimed five lives in Andhra Pradesh, prompting Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu to announce a comprehensive relief and compensation package for affected families, farmers, fishermen and businesses.
Expressing condolences to the bereaved families, he said the government had made extensive efforts to minimise casualties and property damage.

Addressing a press conference at the Secretariat on Wednesday, the Chief Minister identified the deceased as Amrapinni Devmud and Kolamuru Madhavi from the Visakhapatnam region, Chukkala Kishore from Bhimavaram, Bhagyalakshmi from Anakapalli and Kollu Venkayamma from Sakretipalli.
Mr. Devmud died after a tree fell on an electric wire, while Ms. Madhavi died after an electric pole fell on her.
Mr. Kishore was killed when a palm tree fell on him, and Ms. Bhagyalakshmi died of electrocution.
Ms. Venkayamma died when a wall collapsed on her while she was travelling in a passenger vehicle.
The families of each deceased person would receive an ex gratia payment of ₹5 lakh, Mr. Naidu said.
He urged people to remain cautious even after the cyclone crossed the coast.
Families whose houses were inundated would receive 25 kg of rice, while fishermen’s families and handloom households would get 50 kg.
Each affected family would also receive one kg each of red gram, onions, sugar and potatoes, besides one litre of palm oil.
Those staying in relief camps would receive ₹1,000 per person, subject to a ceiling of ₹3,000 per family.
Partially damaged houses would receive ₹10,000 in compensation.

In response to the intensifying system, the weather department has placed 26 districts—including Patna, Jehanabad, Begusarai, Gaya, Khagaria, Lakhisarai, Darbhanga, Madhubani, Saharsa, Samastipur, Supaul, Aurangabad, and both East and West Champaran—under 'Yellow' and 'Orange' alerts. Local farmers face immediate economic risk as the unseasonal rain and overcast conditions cause severe damage to standing paddy crops currently awaiting harvest. The persistent weather system is expected to drive daytime temperatures down further while keeping daily life severely disrupted. The Meteorological Department is closely monitoring the cyclone's trajectory and speed, urging citizens to exercise extreme caution and avoid unnecessary travel during lightning storms and high winds. According to the Meteorological Department, winds will blow at a speed of 50 kmph during this period. Furthermore, a warning has been issued for heavy rainfall accompanied by intense lightning. In light of the advance warning from the Meteorological Department, people are advised to move to safe locations during the adverse weather. article_sentences: At least five people are reportedly feared dead in Andhra Pradesh in the aftermath of Cyclone Arnab, which made landfall on Wednesday, October 28, bringing heavy winds and rain.
Damage to crops, roads, power infrastructure and houses have also been reported in various parts of the state.
Cyclone Arnab crossed the coast near Narsapuram, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam, and towards the Yanam coast, between 2 am and 8 am on October 28.
Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu is set to visit cyclone-affected areas on October 29.
He will inspect damaged crops and interact with farmers in Cheyyeru and Katrenikona villages of Konaseema district.
He will also visit flood-affected individuals taking shelter in cyclone relief centres.

CM Naidu said he spoke with Union Home Minister Amit Shah and briefed him on the impact of Cyclone Arnab on Andhra Pradesh, asking him to send teams from the Union government to assess damage and extend financial assistance.
He mentioned that crops in about 70,900 hectares, mainly paddy, and horticulture crops of over 10,450 hectares have been reported damaged.
“I explained the extensive damage caused by the cyclone, particularly to agricultural and horticultural crops, power infrastructure, roads and other public assets.

In view of the widespread damage, I requested the Union Home Minister to depute Central teams at the earliest to assess the losses and extend financial assistance from the Government of India to support relief, rehabilitation and restoration efforts,” CM Naidu said.
The CM held a teleconference with officials on the morning of October 29, where he was informed that normalcy has returned to most cyclone-affected areas, with the exception of a few locations.
Meanwhile, voting for urban local bodies will also continue as planned earlier on November 1, the State Election Commission has announced.

stories.headline: Water Resources Dept. steps up estuary dredging in Chennai to improve flood water discharge during monsoon
stories.title: Water Resources Dept. steps up estuary dredging in Chennai to improve flood water discharge during monsoon
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: With the first phase of monsoon desilting works in city waterways completed, the Water Resources Department (WRD) is now focusing on dredging estuaries from Pudhupattinam to Pazhaverkadu to clear sand deposits and improve the flow of floodwater into the sea.
The department had started desilting and clearing of floating waste from various waterways in Chennai and its surrounding districts and Cuddalore district at a cost of ₹42 crores in September.
Of the total 528.44 km of waterways in five districts, nearly 104.74 km of waterways lie within the Greater Chennai Corporation limits.
Work is in progress to keep waterways clear of water hyacinth till December end, said officials of the WRD.

With the major rivers and their confluence points with the sea playing a pivotal role in collecting and conveying floodwater, the WRD is now focusing on dredging estuaries at various points of the city and neighbouring districts to improve flood discharge and mitigate inundation.
A total of 17 works are underway along the 20-km long Cooum river.
In the absence of inflow, sand accumulates near the river mouth owing to littoral drift.
Five machines have been deployed to dredge the Cooum estuary and maintain the opening of up to 250 metre.
Sand bars have been cleared up to 120 metre so far, said officials.

The seasonal dredging works are being carried out based on National Institute of Ocean Technology’s recommendations to ensure tidal exchange, maintain biodiversity and flood discharge capacity of the estuaries.

Similarly, works are in progress in Muttukadu, Pudhupattinam and Pazhaverkadu estuaries to improve the depth and width of the estuaries to enable smooth discharge of floodwater into the sea during rainy days.
Accumulated sand deposits have been cleared in 100 metre of the total width of 300 metre in Muttukadu estuary.

stories.title: Supreme Court Refuses To Entertain Challenge To Casual Vacancy Election In Punjab &Haryana Bar Council
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday (October 29) declined to entertain a petition filed by an advocate challenging the Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana's decision to conduct an election to fill up the casual vacancy which arose following the recommendation for the elevation of an elected member as a Judge of the High Court.
A bench comprising Justice Vikram Nath, Justice Sandeep Mehta and Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh heard the petition filed by advocate Chetan Verma.

Verma had approached the Supreme Court challenging an October 9 order passed by Election Tribunal No. 2 at New Delhi, which rejected his plea seeking to be declared a member of the Bar Council against a vacancy that arose after Minderjeet Yadav, an elected member, was elevated as a judge of the Punjab and Haryana High Court.
The appeal was filed under Section 38 of the Advocates Act, 1961.
Verma had contested the Bar Council of Punjab and Haryana elections held in March 2026.
He claimed that he had secured the highest number of votes among the unsuccessful candidates and had not been eliminated during the vote-counting process.
Following the Collegium's recommendation for Yadav's elevation to the High Court, Verma claimed that he was entitled to fill the resulting vacancy.
He argued that the election process had not been fully completed when the vacancy arose.
However, the Election Tribunal rejected his claim, holding that the vacancy was a casual vacancy governed by Rules 45 and 46 of the applicable rules.
It observed that the rules did not provide for the automatic induction of the highest unsuccessful candidate to fill such a vacancy.

The Tribunal held that a casual vacancy among the elected members of the Bar Council had to be filled in accordance with the prescribed procedure, which provides for an election among eligible advocates.
The Tribunal also vacated its interim order restraining the Bar Council from filling the vacancy, permitting it to proceed in accordance with law and the directions issued by the Supreme Court.

reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Wednesday (October 28, 2026) raised India’s concerns over Washington’s support package for Pakistan’s F-16 fighter aircraft with U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth during a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, Philippines.
The two leaders also discussed the threat of cross-border terrorism, with Mr. Hegseth reaffirming Washington’s support to India in combating the menace.

According to the Ministry of Defence, the meeting provided an opportunity to review progress under the India-U.S. Major Defence Partnership, including the implementation of foundational security agreements and avenues to enhance operational readiness, technology sharing and defence industrial integration.
Mr. Singh emphasised the need for a zero-tolerance approach towards countries that support, train or finance terrorist organisations.
He expressed appreciation for the consistent support extended by the U.S. in India’s fight against cross-border terrorism.

Mr. Singh also conveyed to Mr. Hegseth that any transfer of advanced military technology to Pakistan could ultimately result in the technology reaching a third country, raising concerns over its wider proliferation and implications for regional security.

The two Ministers also reviewed the ten-year India-U.S. Defence Framework and discussed strengthening military-to-military exchanges, maritime security cooperation and resilient defence supply chains.
In a post on X, Mr. Singh described the robust India-U.S. partnership as a cornerstone of a free, open and secure Indo-Pacific.
Separately, Mr. Singh held talks with Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi, reviewing progress in bilateral defence cooperation since their meeting in August.

The discussions covered maritime security cooperation, including enhancing mine countermeasure capabilities and exploring joint development in naval shipbuilding and design by combining Japan’s technological expertise with India’s manufacturing capabilities.
The two sides also discussed expanding air force cooperation following the first-ever visit of Japanese fighter aircraft to India for the ‘Veer Guardian 26’ exercise.
They welcomed the India-Japan Defence Industry Forum in Tokyo, which saw participation from around 40 companies.

stories.headline: Who guards India’s digital gatekeepers?
stories.title: Who guards India’s digital gatekeepers?
stories.summary: From the era of submitting application forms in triplicate to today, India has managed something truly remarkable: we have built digital systems that can move money in seconds, verify identities across an enormous population and attempt to bridge our many languages that surprised even the babus.But getting a government officer to answer a telephone remains a challenge. Both realities can co-exist. Our digital achievements deserve recognition. They also deserve scrutiny. The argument begins when we decide what kind of scrutiny is needed.Also read | India’s Arrakis problem: The price of what low-skilled workers knowPundits are out there arguing extensively for using competition law to regulate the digital platforms. When the government builds the digital highway, the sensible response is to demand accountability. Indeed India’s digital gates need opening, but not every lock needs competition law.A government platform is not automatically another Google or Amazon simply because millions of people depend on it. Aadhaar, UPI, DigiYatra and BHASHINI perform different functions, under different obligations, from those of commercial platforms. Some of these systems have made services cheaper and more accessible than a conventional private business might find worthwhile. The State can afford to take a longer-term view as it need not live by QSQT—Quarter Se Quarter Tak. That is a genuine advantage and it’s not a licence to escape accountability.A government system can fail in several ways. An authentication failure that prevents someone from accessing a benefit is an administrative and reliability problem. A platform that unfairly disadvantages private competitors may raise a competition issue. Misuse of personal information belongs in the privacy and data-protection conversation and under the DPDP purview.Refusal to explain a decision raises questions of transparency. These problems overlap, of course. But treating all of them as competition-law violations would be rather like taking every hospital complaint to the Income Tax department because the hospital happens to charge money.Also read | AI could wipe out $200 billion of IT services work by 2030: BCGThere is another uniquely Indian complication. We are very good at producing rules, notifications, circulars and clarifications. Finding out which one applies to a particular problem is another matter. Adding more disclosure requirements may produce impressive document repositories without making life easier for the aam aadmi. The consultants and lawyers will benefited; the citizen may still be standing in a line at the counter.What we need is useful information: how often systems fail, who gets excluded, how complaints are resolved, whether independent audits identify recurring problems and what happens when an institution fails to correct them. No one should be asked to publish everything. That is not what transparency means. Security-sensitive details should not be released simply to demonstrate a commitment to transparency. Nobody sensible would demand that a public infrastructure system publish instructions for hackers to breach. But there is a difference between protecting a vulnerability and protecting an institution from embarrassment. The latter has a habit of borrowing the language of national security.And who checks the people doing the checking? An audit that outsiders cannot meaningfully evaluate risks becoming an institution hiding itself from prying eyes. Exemptions that cannot be challenged can turn temporary secrecy into permanent shelter. Like what we witness now with the Election Commission and SIR.This is where the debate about government digital gatekeepers becomes louder. If private platforms can be scrutinised for favouring their own services or discriminating against competitors, a government-backed platform should not receive a free pass merely because its owner is the State. Recent history has shown us that the State too has its favourites.Since identical institutions don’t exist, equal scrutiny does not make sense. A commercial app store, a public identity database and a payments infrastructure do not necessarily exercise the same powers or carry the same responsibilities. Where a government entity conducts economic activity, competition law may have a legitimate role but when it performs a sovereign function, other accountability mechanisms may be more appropriate. The difficulty is deciding where the boundary lies—and ensuring that the boundary does not become an escape route.Just because an entity carries a government label, the Competition Commission of India should not be denied jurisdiction. Equally, competition law should not be turned into a universal accountability mechanism because other institutions are not doing their jobs. If the existing framework leaves a gap, Parliament and the courts should step in to clarify it.The aam aadmi, meanwhile, is usually missing from these sophisticated arguments on market access, competitive neutrality, regulatory jurisdiction and institutional mandates. The person most affected may simply be trying to complete a transaction or access a service. When the system rejects an application, the distinction between a sovereign function and an economic activity makes no difference to him/her.India needs accessible performance data, independent audits, effective grievance redress and consequences for persistent failure. Security exemptions must be proportionate, and citizens must have a meaningful way to challenge decisions that affect them. Our digital infrastructure is too important to be left unquestioned. It is also too valuable to be weakened by applying the wrong regulatory instrument to every problem.The State should open its digital gates to scrutiny. But the real test of accountability is actually very simple: when something goes wrong, can an aam aadmi get an answer without needing a lawyer, a lobbyist or divine intervention?

article_sentences: The Court observed that in the absence of an existing legal framework, it cannot issue such a direction.

The Supreme Court on Thursday declined to issue a direction to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to mandate full public disclosure of the ultimate beneficial owners (last natural persons) and portfolios of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) and their intermediaries in India.

Citing the lack of an existing legal or regulatory framework, the bench comprising Justice BV Nagarathna, Justice R Mahadevan and Justice DK Upadhyaya disposed of the writ petition filed by Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra.

Advocate Prashant Bhushan, for the petitioner, argued that the lack of public disclosure of the ultimate beneficial owners of these investment vehicles had created opacity in the stock market and enabled potential manipulation.
Bhushan submitted that large sums of money were being invested in Indian companies through foreign entities, but the identity of the actual investors remained unknown.
“These people who are investing into our companies through foreign entities, we don't know who they are and whether they are violating SEBI regulations.
Today there is a lot of suspicion that stock markets are being manipulated by these companies which are investing huge sums,” he said.

He contended that the requirement of disclosing the ultimate beneficial owner, which existed earlier, was given up in 2018, after which entities were only required to comply with the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).

Referring to the observations of the expert committee appointed by the Supreme Court in the Adani-Hindenburg case, Bhushan argued that the removal of the disclosure requirement had weakened the regulatory framework.
He said: “Let's say shares of a company are going up very rapidly and very steeply.

Then some stock broker tells the retail investor that the share is going up, why don't you put money into this share… This person does not know that the reason the share price is going up is because the promoters of that very company are buying the shares through an AIF or an FPI, thereby boosting the share price.
Then he will not buy the share.”

stories.headline: Eastern MP on orange alert as IMD warns of extremely heavy rain
stories.title: Eastern MP on orange alert as IMD warns of extremely heavy rain
stories.summary: Bhopal, Oct 29 : The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange alert for extremely heavy rainfall in parts of eastern Madhya Pradesh on Thursday under the influence of Cyclone Arnab. Mauganj, Sidhi and Singrauli are under the orange alert, while several other districts have been warned of heavy rain and thunderstorms. According to the Meteorological Centre, Bhopal, moderate thunderstorms with lightning and moderate rain are likely to continue over Balaghat, Mandla, Kanha, Dindori, Shahdol, Banagarh Dam, Anuppur, Amarkantak, Sidhi and Singrauli. Thunderstorms with lightning and light rain are expected over Seoni, Jabalpur, Bhedaghat, Katni, Umaria, Bandhavgarh, Satna, Chitrakoot, Maihar, Rewa, Mauganj, Panna, Tikamgarh, Chhatarpur, Khajuraho, Damoh, Narsinghpur, Chhindwara and Pandhurna. The IMD has also indicated the possibility of moderate rain at the rate of 5-15 mm per hour in the orange-alert districts, with a 30-60 per cent chance of cloud-to-ground lightning. In other areas, light rain of less than 5 mm per hour and lower lightning probability are expected. Even after the withdrawal of the monsoon, rainfall activity continues in the state. Weather conditions are likely to deteriorate further in the eastern region on Thursday. Heavy rain is also expected in Rewa, Satna, Maihar, Shahdol, Umaria, Anuppur, Dindori, Mandla and Balaghat, with some places possibly receiving four inches or more of rain. Cities such as Bhopal, Gwalior, Raisen, Sehore, Rajgarh, Vidisha, Shajapur, Dewas, Narmadapuram, Betul, Harda, Guna, Shivpuri, Datia, Ashoknagar, Morena, Bhind and Sheopur may witness cloudy skies, light rain, strong winds and thunderstorms. The IMD has advised people to stay away from low-lying areas, avoid shelter under trees during thunderstorms and exercise caution while travelling on wet roads. The southwest monsoon withdrew from Madhya Pradesh on October 3, yet rainfall has continued throughout the month due to weather systems distinct from typical monsoon patterns, including the influence of a cyclone in the Bay of Bengal. Weather experts note that data from the past decade shows October can bring a mix of rain, heat and cold. The month has witnessed bright sunshine and clear skies, but a drop in nighttime temperatures has been accompanied by rain in several districts. The southwest monsoon remained active for about 100 days, and even after its withdrawal, localised systems are sustaining the ongoing rainfall. --IANS

stories.title: Jio Platforms set for steady Q2 growth; tariff hikes remain in focus
stories.summary: Two days after its public-market debut, Jio Platforms faces a crucial quarterly test as limited Arpu growth leaves investors seeking clarity on future price increases.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Jio Platforms Ltd is set to announce its July-September quarter earnings on Friday, just two days after its stellar public-market debut.

The company is expected to report stable earnings for the quarter on the back of continued subscriber additions, traction in the home broadband segment, and growth in digital services, according to analysts.

The performance will test the growth potential of Jio’s average revenue per user (Arpu), which is expected to remain limited as the company has refrained from raising tariffs, unlike rival Bharti Airtel, which recently discontinued its entry-level ₹299 plan and increased postpaid tariffs.
“While Bharti withdrew its low-value plans, there was no follow up by other players and we are still awaiting tariff increase by the sector,” analysts at Emkay wrote in a note dated 6 October.
In the July-September quarter, Jio is expected to post nearly 2% quarter-on-quarter Arpu growth to ₹219.5, according to average estimates from four brokerage firms.
Analysts expect the ₹300 Jio Prime membership fee introduced in August, which protects users from tariff hikes until 5 September 2027, to provide additional revenue support in the interim.
“With recent postpaid tariff hikes by Bharti, JPL’s (Jio Platforms’) listing, and Vi (Vodafone Idea) being close to securing a debt raise, we believe smartphone tariff hikes are imminent.
We model a 15% smartphone tariff hike in March 2027,” analysts at Motilal Oswal said in a note dated 28 October.
When the company reports its earnings, investors will be watching closely for guidance on the next headline tariff hike.
Operators have so far relied on 2G-to-4G and 4G-to-5G upgrades, higher postpaid additions, and rising data usage to sustain growth without major pricing action.
However, rising smartphone prices could temper handset upgrades and weaken this premiumisation trend.
